chapter: Boston, Buffalo and finding a style
title: Studying harmony and asking musicians to play notes for him
summary: He studied harmony in Boston, then kept learning by having musicians play notes for him and by working out bass lines with pianists.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Now, at that time, now, were you studying harmony with anyone at that time?
Yes, when I went to Boston, I studied

harmony also.
You studied harmony at Boston.
Yeah.
But now, after you left, after you left Boston, did you continue with your studies?
Well --
I don't necessarily mean formally but --

No, not formally, of course, but I still, like I said, I had a very good ear, and I kept practicing. How did I go about it? Like lots of times I got into a sort of a thing with a couple of the musicians. I asked them to hit a couple of the notes for me on their instrument or on the piano, and I'd see if I could hit the note, what note they are hitting. I used to do that with Art Tatum years and years --
Later.
-- later.
Now, what were you doing at that, you know, at this time in the early part of your career, the mid-'30s? Were you still, were you asking people to play things for you then too?
Yes, oh, yes.
Uh-huh. Were you -- did you -- were you working out, like say, were you getting together like with any of the piano players or other bass players that you remember at

that time, working on like different kinds of ways to get to different kinds of harmonic areas, so to speak. Like, for instance, I mean like Ray Brown said once in an interview that he was playing with Charlie Parker. It was either Charlie Parker or Coleman Hawkins. He and the piano player, whose name I don't recall at this moment, used to get together and work out different ways they'd come. They'd take the chorus to the bridge or something.
Yes, right.
Then when Hawkins would come on the job, they'd have something different for him every night.
Right. Sure. Right.
You know, did you do that with any, any particular bassist that you, bassists or piano players or guitarist?
Piano players, especially Art Tatum later on, you know. That was --
But I mean then, though.

Then I used to even, when I worked first in Boston with Dean Earl, the basic notes I somehow just happened to go along with the pattern, you know what I mean. I could hear bass real good, especially would get together with the pianist and find out how he does his bass, which helped quite a bit, and passing tones and the proper bass to be fed to the different choruses that we played.
